Pocketry · 6 November 2026

Tool outlines, before and after

Ten photos of tools on white Pocketry calibration sheets, followed by two wood-background checks. The same crop appears in both columns: the original detector in magenta, and the new default Automatic mode in green. No hand edits, symmetry or photo-specific sensitivity tuning.

We tested color-mask refinement with GrabCut, learned edges with TEED, and line/curve reconstruction. The result combines automatic background selection, guarded learned outlines and sensitivity, local reference-strip handling, and optional outline simplification. Editable curves stays off by default.

How to read this comparison

Before uses Pocketry’s original color detector from commit 6b9eb60a, before the GrabCut, TEED and reconstruction changes. After uses the current Automatic default: light neutral paper selects Tool edges, while other or uncertain backgrounds select Color contrast with guarded GrabCut. Unreliable learned outlines fall back to color detection. The caption names the method actually chosen.

Both versions receive identical perspective-corrected crop pixels and default sensitivity (Auto), simplification and smoothing. Interior holes and Editable curves are off. These are initial detected boundaries: Auto-simplify is a separate preview, and clearance is excluded. Amber marks an estimated edge hidden by a reference strip.

Times are medians of three fresh detections on a Mac using Node 22 and the shipped CPU/WASM runtime. They include inference but exclude photo loading, calibration and downloads. The OpenCV runtime is already initialized. These are desktop measurements, not phone timings or physical-fit validation.

These selected examples show improvements and remaining limitations; they are not a contour-accuracy benchmark. Full source photos are not included; report crops omit EXIF metadata.
